==Problem==
A whole number larger than <math>2</math> leaves a remainder of <math>2</math> when divided by each of the numbers <math>3, 4, 5,</math> and <math>6</math>. The smallest such number lies between which two numbers?

<math>\textbf{(A)}\ 40\ \text{and}\ 49 \qquad \textbf{(B)}\ 60 \text{ and } 79 \qquad \textbf{(C)}\ 100\ \text{and}\ 129 \qquad \textbf{(D)}\ 210\ \text{and}\ 249\qquad \textbf{(E)}\ 320\ \text{and}\ 369</math>

==Solution==
The smallest number divisible by <math>3,4,5,</math> and <math>6</math>, or their least common multiple, can be found to be <math>60</math>. When <math>2</math> is added to a multiple of number, its remainder when divided by that number is <math>2</math>. The number we are looking for is therefore <math>62</math>, and between <math>\boxed{\textbf{(B)}\ 60\ \text{and}\ 79}</math>.
